title: Are CPAT's Price Elasticities Right?
subtitle: A check of the defaults against meta-analyses and reviews
message: Seven of ten fuel-sector defaults lie within the published range. Three are too high, and road gasoline is double the estimate corrected for publication bias. Two structural choices matter more: the full long-run response in one year, and no cross-price terms.

problem.title: One table sets the size of every cut

stats.label: fuel-sector pairs within the published range
industrial diesel and services gasoline, against −0.4 to −0.8
road gasoline against the bias-corrected mean (−0.64 vs −0.31)

problem.text: If an elasticity is twice the true value, CPAT reports twice the cut and overstates how fast the tax base erodes. Nobody had published a fuel-by-fuel check of the defaults.

mechanism.title: Most defaults pass; timing does not
mechanism.caption: Own-price elasticity by horizon: CPAT (dashed) against partial adjustment (solid).
points: After one year about a fifth of CPAT's response has happened; after five, about 60%.
No cross-price terms: almost no fuel switching outside power.
The Total Effective Carbon Price moves by only about a tenth.

action.title: Fix three values and the timing
results: Front-loading overstates near-term cuts and understates early revenue.
Common errors cancel in the TECP.
